To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the magnitude of the weak phase phi(2) is consistent with the standard-model prediction from B -> pi(+)pi (-) and B -> rho(+)pi(-), (ii) its sign is not determined by the current experimental data, and (iii) the penguin pollution in the pi(0)pi(0) mode is not yet determined.

the magnitude of the CP-violation parameter alpha (or phi (2)), which has been determined from the indirect measurements of B -> pi(+)pi (-) and B -> pi(0)pi(0), agrees with the standard-model expectations.

the weak phase alpha is in the range of (50 degrees) to (130 degrees) with a central value of (85 degrees) at 68% confidence level, and that the QCD penguin contribution is small, i.e. less than 20% at 68% C.L.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the weak phases in the standard-model parameterization of B -> pi(pi) transitions, which is a crucial step towards a better understanding of CP violation in B decays.
the determination of the weak angle gamma in B decays, and in particular, with the extraction of the CP-violating weak phase alpha (phi(2)) from B -> pi pi and other B -> P P decays (P = pi, K).

the following issues: (i) The extraction of alpha (or) phi(2) in the standard model; (ii) A comparison between our model-independent results and the predictions based on QCD factorization and perturbative QCD approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the world averages of current data on B -> pi pi and B -> rho rho decays are not sufficient to provide a model-independent determination of alpha (or the QCD penguin contributions) and to resolve the discrete ambiguity in the determination of alpha.
the present data do not yet allow for a reliable determination of the weak phases alpha (or phi2) and gamma (or phi3) in B -> pi(pi) decays.
the current data are consistent with alpha (or phi (2)) = 0, which is a standard-model prediction, but they cannot rule out a nonzero value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with the current experimental data, the isospin analysis of B -> pi(+)pi (-) and B -> pi(0)pi(0) decays can provide a more stringent constraint on the QCD penguin amplitude, and thus on alpha (or phi (2)), than the direct CP asymmetry in the pi(0) pi(0) channel, which is the only direct measurement of alpha (or) phi(2) at present.

the present experimental data are consistent with a small QCD penguin contamination, but the situation is still not clear and the data are not sufficient to exclude the possibility of a significant QCD penguin contribution.
the present experimental data are not yet sufficient to determine alpha (or phi (2)) and to quantify the QCD penguin contribution in B -> pi(+)pi (-) decays.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the isospin analysis of the B -> pi pi modes provides a powerful tool for the determination of the weak phases alpha and phi(2), which are crucial for the extraction of the CKM angle gamma and the measurement of the unitarity triangle angle beta.
the current experimental data do not allow us to distinguish between the standard-model and the new physics contributions in B -> pi(+)pi(0) decays.
the current experimental data on B -> pi pi modes do not provide any significant constraint on the QCD penguin contributions in B -> pi(+)pi(0) and B -> pi(0)pi(0) decays.
